selection_rationale: The 2027 policy and investment horizon joins a 2026 high-rate monetary cycle, legislated CBS rollout, draft 2027 budget, provisionally applicable EU–Mercosur trade terms, new US trade barriers, Chinese commodity demand and persistent structural productivity constraints.
contrary_evidence: Forecasts range from 1.2% to 2.3% real GDP growth using different institutions, dates and model assumptions; none is a realised 2027 figure.
The 2027 draft budget's R$83.4 billion adjusted primary surplus differs from its R$18.6 billion full primary balance and should not be treated as the same fiscal outcome.
The EU–Mercosur interim trade agreement has been provisionally applied to Brazil since 1 May 2026, but measured investment and export effects require subsequent evidence.
China's large bilateral trade surplus does not identify Brazilian industrial competitiveness or future commodity prices.
BRICS payment interoperability and local-currency settlement are not a common currency or a unified capital market.
limitations: The 2027 budget remains a proposal as of the information cutoff; neither appropriation nor project pipeline constitutes executed spending.
2026 data from GDP, credit, fiscal and trade statistics have different observation dates and should not be presented as one synchronized monthly release.
GDP forecast vintages are shown for comparison, not as a statistical confidence interval or political performance ranking.
Underlying financial and market figures are from public institutional reporting and do not include firm-by-firm audited financial statements.
Conditional scenarios are not assigned subjective probabilities or invented GDP levels.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 3 November 2026, São Paulo civil date. Observed macro series latest from 2026 Q2/September depending on release; 3 November Focus vintage.
producer_checks.research_depth: Portuguese 84,405 characters / 11,223 substantive whitespace tokens; English 77,105 characters / 9,746 substantive whitespace tokens; 35 analytical chapters plus numbered bibliography in each version.
producer_checks.evidence_inventory: 30 unique source URLs across 17 distinct domains per language; includes IBGE, BCB, Finance Ministry, National Treasury, Senate IFI, IMF, World Bank, EU Council, MDIC, BRICS, ANBIMA, BNDES and EPE.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Three comparable bilingual charts: 2027 GDP growth forecasts [1.2,1.4,1.7,2.2,2.3]; observed selected 2026 Selic targets [15,14.75,14.5,14.25,14,13.75]; 2026 Jan–Sep selected export destinations [84.68,44.15,27.46,11.58]. Each language also has a cross-market exposure map, two-way fiscal and monetary transmission flow, and multi-variable empirical and scenario tables.
producer_checks.translation_parity: Thirty-five matching analytical chapters; same first-order economic conclusions, quantifications, fiscal distinctions, dated observations and chart numerical arrays in both editions. Source URL inventories identical.
producer_checks.methodology: Separate observed 2026 data from published 2027 projections and conditional scenarios; use comparable units and periods; do not equate adjusted and full fiscal results; compare national and IMF debt definitions only with caveats; distinguish provisional trade rules from realised outcomes.
producer_checks.source_check: Primary institutional reporting screened through dated source pages. Independent claim-to-source factual QA and publication approval still required.
producer_checks.editorial_status: Staged producer manuscript only, awaiting independent QA; no public reports bundle, build, deployment or publication claimed.
